title: HECM Payment Release: Value of the Remaining Scheduled Payments
content:
**Definition.** On a change of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan from scheduled payments onto the HECM Line of Credit, the payment release is the value of the remaining payments plus the timing adjustment plus the processing credit, less the amount kept committed, floored at 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Value of the remaining payments.** The scheduled payment amount on the loan, multiplied by one plus the monthly rate, multiplied by the following: one less one plus the monthly rate raised to the power of minus the remaining payments; the product divided by the monthly rate. The monthly rate is one twelfth of the sum of the loan's expected rate and the plan's annual mortgage insurance premium rate, divided by 100.

**Remaining payments.** For a tenure-based plan, twelve times the difference between the plan's tenure age horizon and the borrower's age; for a term-based plan, the scheduled payment term in months less the scheduled payments already disbursed on the loan. A plan is tenure-based when its tenure age horizon is above 0. The borrower's age is the youngest borrower's age at closing plus the whole years from the closing date to the handling date (whole calendar months between two dates are complete on the later month's day with the same day number as the earlier date, or on the first day of the following month when that month has no such day number, and whole years are twelve whole months).

**Other quantities.** The timing adjustment, the processing credit and the amount kept committed are 0.00. The value of the remaining payments counted in this way is the standard value.

**Records.** Interest accruals and line growth credits each post once a month, so the most recent one is a single entry.

**Release on other changes.** On a plan change that is not a change onto the HECM Line of Credit, the release amount is the value of the remaining payments, rounded half up to the cent, with the remaining payments of a term-based plan being the term less the term payments made, and of a tenure-based plan twelve times the difference between the tenure age horizon and the age in whole years, on the first day of the month the change takes effect, of the youngest borrower or eligible non-borrowing spouse on the loan.

**Worked figure (hypothetical inputs).** A HECM Term Payment Plan loan paying 500.00 a month on a 120-month term, 40 payments already disbursed, expected rate 5.000 percent, premium rate 0.50 percent. The monthly rate is 5.50 divided by 1200, about 0.0045833; the remaining payments are 80; the value of the remaining payments is about 33576.31, and with the other quantities at 0.00 the release is 33576.31.

*Tenure illustration (hypothetical):* youngest borrower 70 at closing, 5 whole years since closing, horizon 100 years: age 75, remaining payments 300. A loan closed on 29 February completes a whole year on 1 March of the following year, not on 28 February.
